text.p: Grain and oilseed exports reported by USDA and private export sources.
CORN SALE - Taiwan's FGEP corn-buying group bought a shipment of 54,000 tonnes of U.S. No.2 corn from Mitsui at a tender on Wednesday for November delivery, traders said.

WHEAT SALE - Three Philippine firms bought 35,000 tonnes of U.S. soft winter wheat rejected by China at $192 per tonne, including cost and freight, traders said on Wednesday. Traders said the price was a significant discount to the prevailing $230 per tonne for soft winter wheat.

VEGOIL SALE - India's STC bought 12,000 tonnes of RBD palm olein on Tuesday. The STC purchased 6,000 tonnes of RBD palm olein at $586 a tonne for first-half October shipment from Malaysia's FELDA. It also took the other 6,000 tonnes of the same product, paying $581 a tonne for last-half November shipment from Kuok Oils and Grains, traders said.

WHEAT BRAN TENDER - Egyptian state company Misr Oil and Soap said on Wednesday it was postponing until further notice the process of opening bids for 30,000 tonnes of wheat bran pellets. The previous deadline for bids was Wednesday.

WHEAT TENDER - Egypt's official commodities buyer said on Wednesday he was seeking 50,000 tonnes of soft red French wheat for loading at a French port between October 15 and 31. The last date for submitting bids was September 13 at 0700 GMT. Bids should be valid until September 15 at 1000 GMT.

- Syria's General Establishment for Cereal Processing and Trade offered 100,000 tonnes of hard amber durum wheat for sale for November shipment. October 1 was the final date for offers. Confirmation would be made on October 2.

WHEAT TENDER - A Philippine flour mill rejected bids for 35,000 tonnes of U.S. spring wheat for October delivery on Wednesday due to high prices. Philippine flour mills have bought 101,900 tonnes of U.S. wheat, including 35,000 tonnes of soft winter wheat rejected by China, since last week, traders said.

- Algeria has launched a tender for the import of 100,000 tonnes of U.S. and/or Canadian durum wheatfor shipment between the second half of October and the first half of December, European grain traders said. Results are expected by the end of the week, they said.
WHEAT TENDERS - The CCC will tender on Sept 12 for 8,000 tonnes of U.S. SRW wheat for donation to Jamaica.
- The CCC said it is seeking 25,000 tonnes of U.S. hard red winter wheat under the export donation program for Bosnia. Shipment is set for Oct 5-31 and bids are due on September 17.
- The CCC seeks on Sept 10 19,860 tonnes of soft white wheat of which 15,340 is for donation to Ethiopia and 4,520 for Pakistan for Sept 25-Oct 20 shipment.
- The CCC seeks up to 4,410 tonnes of U.S. No.2 soft red winter or soft white wheat for donation to Senegal. Shipment period is set for October 5-31 and offers are due by Sept 18.

WHEAT TENDERS - The CCC seeks 23,500 tonnes of U.S. wheat for donation to Honduras. The deal includes 5,000 tonnes NS/DNS wheat and 3,000 tonnes soft red winter wheat set for November 1-25 shipment. It also includes 9,500 NS/DNS wheat and 6,000 tonnes SRW wheat for Dec 10-30. Offers due Sept 11.
CORN TENDER - Jordan is to seek 50,000 tonnes of U.S. No. 3 yellow corn for shipment in first half of November. Offers must be received by September 25.
- The CCC seeks up to 4,280 tonnes of U.S. No. 2 yellow corn under the export donation program to Angola. Shipment period is slated for Oct 5-31 and offers are due by Sept 18.
RICE TENDER - Ivory Coast will seek 29,000 tonnes of PL-480 long grain brown rice for Oct 15-Nov 15 and/or Nov 15-Dec 15 shipment. Bids are due by Sept 11.

MARKET TALK - USDA Secretary Dan Glickman warned that the U.S. will subsidize its grain exports if the EU or other exporters launch new export subsidies ... The EU played down on the warning from Glickman, saying that a trade war was unlikely under present market conditions.
... The one million tonnes of corn rotting in storage in China's port of Dalian will lead to tightened local supplies and force prices up before new crop is available at year-end.
--Doris Frankel 312-983-7305
